<thought>We have the 13C NMR signals: 161.40, 143.85, 130.30, 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm. Aromatic carbons usually appear between about 110–160 ppm. The three downfield signals (161.40, 143.85, 130.30) fall in that region, while the remaining four are aliphatic. Even though 161.40 is near the upper edge and could correspond to a carbonyl, without additional data we assume it is an aromatic carbon (e.g., a substituted aromatic carbon). Therefore the molecule contains **3 aromatic carbons**.</thought>
<final_answer>3</final_answer>
